SEARCH
Package org.yuemi.mmoaccessories.api

Interface AccessoriesApi

public interface AccessoriesApi
Public API for managing player accessories (equipment slots).

An accessory slot is identified by an AccessorySlot (or a custom slot id when the slot is defined in config.yml). Items are validated against the slot's accepted-types via MMO Items (MmoItemsApi.getItemTypes).

Equip / unequip events flow through MMO Mechanics' MmoMechanicsApi.fireTrigger(UUID, "onEquip"/"onUnequip") so any skill declaring a matching trigger in its JSON5 triggers[] list runs as part of the same logical operation. In-slot triggers (e.g. onAttack on a worn ring) are dispatched by the accessories plugin's EventApi-subscribed listener through MmoMechanicsApi.castSkill.

Storage is pluggable via the AccessoryStorage SPI. The default backend is pdc (player PersistentDataContainer); sqlite, mysql and mongodb are optional backends. Select the backend in config.yml under storage.type.

  • Method Details

    • equipAccessory

      boolean equipAccessory(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull AccessorySlot slot, int slotIndex, @NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack item)
      Equip item to (slot, slotIndex) for player.

      Returns false if any precondition fails:

      • slotIndex is out of range for the slot's max-slots.
      • !canEquipToSlot(item, slot).
      • The item cannot be resolved to a stored id (no MMO Items id and no vanilla material fallback).

      On success the access is persisted, then the onEquip trigger is dispatched through MMO Mechanics.

      Parameters:
      player - the target player
      slot - which accessory slot
      slotIndex - zero-based index inside the slot (must be < max-slots)
      item - the item to place in the slot
      Returns:
      true if the item was successfully equipped

    • unequipAccessory

      boolean unequipAccessory(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull AccessorySlot slot, int slotIndex)
      Remove the accessory at (slot, slotIndex) for player.

      On success the onUnequip trigger is dispatched through MMO Mechanics.

      Returns:
      true if a slot was actually cleared (i.e. the slot was non-empty); false if the slot index was out of range or the slot was already empty

    • getEquipped

      @NotNull @NotNull Optional<org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack> getEquipped(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull AccessorySlot slot, int slotIndex)
      Read back the equipped item at (slot, slotIndex).

      The returned item is reconstructed from the storage id (so a freshly-spawned item will be a new instance, not a reference to whatever the player had when equipped).

      Returns:
      the item, or empty if the slot is empty / out of range / the stored id can't be resolved

    • getAllEquipped

      @NotNull @NotNull List<org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack> getAllEquipped(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Read back every equipped accessory for player, across all slots.

      The list contains only non-empty slots and preserves slot ordering (BELT, GLOVES x max, RING x max, NECKLACE). Empty slots are skipped.

    • canEquipToSlot

      boolean canEquipToSlot(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack item, @NotNull @NotNull AccessorySlot slot)
      Check whether item can be placed in slot.

      Returns true when the item's MMO Items types (read via MmoItemsApi.getItemTypes(item)) include any of the slot's accepted-types entries. Falls back to a material-name match when MMO Items isn't installed or returns an empty type list.
